title: Draft: Reload file when reloading lua plugins if loaded by lua file handler
description:
Update: Please see !4311 for a better approach.

This is still a work-in-progress - as far as I can tell, this works for me, but I'm not intimately familiar with the Wireshark internals and I've only tested with custom file readers, not custom file writers. Feedback on the best approach to take would be much appreciated.

This merge request tries to address #17615 by enhancing the reload lua plugin function to check if the capture file is using a lua file handler. If it is, it reloads the capture file after reloading lua plugins but before performing dissection again. This clears out the old deregistered file handler instance that is no longer functional and gives the lua file handler a chance to run again cleanly to provide packets to dissect.

If the current file is modified, it also prompts to save before proceeding with the lua reload, the same as if the lua `reload_packets()` command was run.

In order to facilitate the check for whether a lua file handler is in use, I added a new `wtap_uses_lua()` API function that tests if `wslua_data` is non-null. As far as I can tell, `wslua_data` is currently only used to store the lua FileHandler instance and is otherwise always null for non-lua-based readers.

This solution has the drawback that the current frame position is lost when reloading a file using a custom lua file handler, but given that previously it was impossible to reload the file without manually reopening it anyways, I think it's still a useful improvement.

notes.body:
> This solution has the drawback that the current frame position is lost when reloading a file using a custom lua file handler, but given that previously it was impossible to reload the file without manually reopening it anyways, I think it's still a useful improvement.

This is only ever an issue before loading the right Lua script. e.g. you start dissecting your companies profile, but forgot to copy the Lua script to the right place, copying and reloading will now jump to the beginning of the trace file. It seems to be a nuisance at first, but actually dissection could change the position you want to look at anyway, so I wouldn't mind this change.

What I do think should be done though is, that this needs to be configurable. It should be avoided to change the systems behavior between major updates, without having an option to get the old functionality back. Now this change will not be made for 3.6 (as the train for that has left the station already), but 3.8 or 4.0 depending on what we are going to number the next release. Because of that I think it is ok to change default behavior, but we might need a way of using a config option to get the old behavior back.

TLDR; this needs to be a preference option, but it could be an expert one.

@stigbjorlykke @geraldcombs - what do you guys think?

This is also an issue when **developing** the Lua script, which is why we also jump to the selected frame. But, as you say, changing a file reader may change the frames so it may not be a real issue.

@rknall Why do we need a configuration for this? I don't see any behaviour to keep here, if I understand correctly our current implementation will fail anyway.

I agree that this is likely to be an issue during development, which is the main reason why I've been working with this feature.

I could try to implement something that would save the selected frame number before reloading and try to jump to it afterwards if the index is still in bounds as a best-effort thing.

@stigbjorlykke it was just the general question I was raising. It does change behavior, and we tend to be on the conservative side with that stuff. If I understood it correctly, the current implementation will not fail, just behave differently.

I am fine with it not having preferences.
I made a different solution in !4311 which will not reload the file, so hopefully we will not need to change the behaviour.

@rknall I didn't manage to make a good solution without reloading the file (as you indicated). When thinking about it I found one use case for having a preference to turn off reloading: When using a Lua FileHandler and also developing a Lua Dissector for the packets, and no changes are done to the FileHandler. Using this preference may give undesirable results because changing the FileHandler has no effect after reload, so I think we should not have it.

btw; This bugfix should be backported to older versions.
nit: iff -> if

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/4304/diffs?diff_id=251313574&start_sha=69ff0160f08a1f28aff8679378de4a2c66db6de0#a7750c0ac3288e0c93b456bb0f274776b3809458_1835_1835)

I've reworded it to use "if and only if" instead of using the "iff" short-hand.

It's an important distinction that I don't want to lose, since it's critical to the correctness that checking for a non-null `wslua_data` is logically equivalent to checking for a lua file handler. (If this isn't true now, or becomes false later, then this function will need to be fixed/updated).
I didn't know about the iff abbreviation, and because of this I think it's better to write "if and only if".

Yes, I agree that it is better to write it out in full. I had originally used the abbreviated form because it made it all fit on one line, but clarity is more important than making the comment compact.
When doing `cf_reload()` it should not be needed to do `fieldsChanged()` and `redissectPackets()` after reloading. I think you should do either one or the two others.
Thanks, I've updated it accordingly.
After a closer look at the functionality I don't think `cf_reload()` will do the correct work for now, and this may be a bigger task to fix (based on your analysis).

I don't have a macos device to test with, but I'll try building and running under Linux to see if I can reproduce it there. It looks like it must be the "Unregistered hf! index" assertion, but I'm still familiarizing myself with that part of the code.

Okay, I can trigger the assertion reliably if I add a colorization rule that depends upon a field provided by a lua dissector, though I'm sure there are other ways to trigger it.

It looks like it's maybe some sort of race condition between activity kicked off by the capture file read finished event like colorization rules or column info population and the re-registration of the lua dissectors?

After some debugging, I've gleaned a better understanding of some of the behavior, but there's still a lot that I don't fully understand.

1. `wslua_reload_plugins()` deregisters the protocol fields associated with lua plugins, but it doesn't immediately free them because they might still be in use, instead, it puts them into a list of deregistered fields to clean up later.
2. Normally, that happens when `redissectPackets()` calls `proto_free_deregistered_fields()` at the end of the whole reload process.
3. However, in the modified flow I introduced, I reload the capture file which closes the capture file via `cf_close()` and eventually runs `cleanup_dissection()` for `epan` which dispatches cleanup functions. One of the cleanup functions is `http2_cleanup_protocol()`, which directly calls `proto_free_deregistered_fields()`, freeing those deregistered fields earlier than usual.
4. `cf_reload()` eventually runs callbacks for the read/reload event completion, triggering UI refreshes that attempt to use deregistered fields that have since been freed, triggering the assertion.

I can prevent it from tripping the assertion if I comment out the call to `proto_free_deregistered_fields()` in `http2_cleanup_protocol()`. Of course, it's still necessary to call `proto_free_deregistered_fields()` after reloading the file by some other means, either directly or via `redissectPackets()`. However, if I do call `proto_free_deregistered_fields()` immediately after `cf_reload()`, it still triggers the assert later, so maybe that's still too early.

As an experiment, I tried omitting the call to `proto_free_deregistered_fields()` entirely, leaking those fields but removing the question of whether anything is freed too early. It doesn't assert, unsurprisingly, but the colorization rule doesn't get reapplied correctly after reloading the lua plugins. That suggests that there's probably further interaction between those post-read/reload UI events and the deregistered fields that I'm not properly handling.
It didn't really work updating `wth->wslua_data` to avoid a full reload, but MR !4311 is updated to do either redissect or reload. And it fixes the memory leak from FileHandler.
Yeah, !4311 seems to work pretty well now, so I'll close this merge request in favor of 4311.

commits_data.title: WIP: reload file if loaded by lua file handler
commits_data.message:
WIP: reload file if loaded by lua file handler

Prevent certain failure when reloading lua plugins when the capture
file was loaded by a custom lua file handler. When reloading a
capture file from a lua file handler, reload the file before
redissecting the packets. Otherwise the deregistered FileHandler
will throw an error when rereading the packets for dissection.

Add a new wtap_uses_lua() API function to check if the current file
in the wiretap session is using a lua file handler.
